newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 21.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's The Wall Street Journal:
* Boeing Co's plans to cancel building larger 747s raises the possibility that Airbus Industrie will proceed with its A-3XX aircraft.
* Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc chief executive resigns.
* Boston Scientific Corp agrees to acquire Target Therapeutics Inc in a stock deal valued at $1.1 billion.
* PIMCO Advisors LP is in discussions to buy a one-third interest in Oppenheimer Capital LP from Oppenheimer Group Inc for about $275 million, people familiar with the matter say.
* Banc One Corp confirms it will buy First USA Inc for $6.65 billion. Stocks of other credit card firms surge, indicating Wall street expects other deals.
* Technology stocks rise on strong earnings. Nasdaq closes at 1,364.28 and the Dow Jones industrials close at 6,843.87.
* Tokyo shares fall 3.4 percent Monday over continuing worries about Japan's economy.
* Officials say the Food and Drug Administration may issue a ruling to let Quaker Oats Co and other companies make health claims about oat bran.
* PaineWebber Group Inc, Alex. Brown Inc and Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette release strong fourth quarter earnings.
* A federal judge may reject a pact over additional Nasdaq reforms.
* Dow Jones & Co Inc reported flat fourth quarter profits and said it will spend up to $650 million to bolster its financial information unit.
* A study finds stocks of venture capital-backed firms that had initial public offerings last year rose 13 percent, trailing the Dow Jones industrials.
* Ing C Olivetti & C SpA has a preliminary pact with Britain's Centenary Corp and other investors to sell its personal computer unit.

* Today International Business Machines Corp breaks with yet another of its traditions: Instead of announcing its earnings before the stock market opens, it will do so after the close. -- Heard on the Street.

* The Treasury gets an early indication today of just how much investors are willing to pay for protection against inflation. After the Treasury this morning discloses the size of its first offering of 10-year government notes designed specifically to guard against inflation, the notes will begin trading immediately in what is known as the "when-issued" market. The notes won't actually be sold until January 29.
